why: The criterion holds for both briefs. I checked every command in them against the repository. Every file they name exists at this commit: bin/csv2json.js, src/parse.js, test/csv.test.js, README.md and package.json. `npm test` maps to the "test": "node --test" script. In check 5, `printf '[{"a\\tb":"1\\t2"}]\n'` inside single quotes prints a literal backslash-t, which is the JSON tab escape the output should contain. The verifier says to use bash, so the `cmp - <(...)` process substitution is valid. `grep -n -- '--tsv' test/*.js` and the same grep on README.md are valid. The builder's JavaScript (`process.argv.slice(2)`, `parse(text, '\t')`, and the escaped test strings) is valid. `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv` is an example for the README, not a command to run. The advisory `node bin/csv2json.js x --tsv` has no input piped in, so run alone it would wait on stdin. It is only an example idea outside PASS/FAIL, so I don't count it as a broken command.
